newsitem.title: USA: CME live cattle futures close mostly higher.
newsitem.headline: CME live cattle futures close mostly higher.

text.p: CME live cattle futures finished mostly higher on support generated by talk that wholesale beef prices will bottom soon and on concern over severe weather forecast for early next week, traders said.

Although choice boxed beef values were lower again at midday, select beef prices rose and the volume of trade, reported by USDA at 263 loads of fabricated cuts, continued to be fairly large. This prompted further talk that beef values will be bottoming soon and may rebound somewhat on post-holiday demand.
Also, weather concerns remained in the market which combined with the beef talk, resulted in ideas cash cattle prices would be firmer next week, they said.
Futures slipped to technical support early before drifting back on mixed support, partly following the rally in hog futures. Spreaders bought February which added to gains in that month, they added.
R.J. O'Brien and E.D.&F. Man bought December late while Cargill Investor Services sold. Cargill bought February along with E.D.&F. Man and RBH, pit sources said.
Live cattle closed 0.175 cent a lb higher to 0.100 lower with February up most at 63.875 cents.
